implement.summary: Gap on BASE_SHA (INFERRED from code): tools/macos-ci/simulator-launch-check.sh (the only simulator step scripts/mac-full-verify.sh runs, mac-full-verify.sh line ~`simulator-launch-check.sh "$UDID" "$BUNDLE_ID" "$APP_PATH" ...`) only proves launch survival — it installs, launches once, screenshots, checks the pid after SETTLE_SECONDS, scans crash reports and the -34018 entitlement string in the unified log (simulator-launch-check.sh:118-190 on base). Nothing on the Mac plane ever stored wallet contents through the shipping Keychain wallet (apps/mobile/ios/LocalPods/PickleNative/Sources/PickleOfflineWallet.swift -> native/vision-core/Sources/OfflineWallet.swift KeychainOfflineWalletStore, service com.picklesensei.offline.wallet, kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly), killed the process and read them back, so 'wallet persistence across kill' had no evidence at all; base launch-summary.txt has no wallet field. Fix (all inside write_paths tools/macos-ci/): (1) tools/macos-ci/wallet-probe.m — an Objective-C dylib compiled per run for the iPhoneSimulator SDK (app's own archs + MinimumOSVersion), ad-hoc signed, injected via SIMCTL_CHILD_DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES into the installed Release app; inside the process it resolves the real `PickleOfflineWallet` RN module (NSClassFromString) and calls its exported selectors loadWallet/replaceWallet/clearWallet/discardCorruptWallet exactly as the bridge does (so the bytes reaching the Keychain are the product's sealed envelopes under the same certificate-free signature), with a `store` phase (load, discard known-unreadable leftover state, replace at the loaded revision) and a `restore` phase (load, clear at the read-back revision, load again → must be empty), each writing a JSON result atomically and logging under the `PickleWalletProbe` tag. (2) tools/macos-ci/wallet-persistence-check.sh — compiles/signs the probe, stops the running instance, starts a unified log stream, generates a fresh non-secret payload in the exact validated shape (canonical UUID owner, ES256-length compact JWS grant, `result` receipt, nonce per run), launches the store phase, waits for its result while requiring the app and log stream alive, screenshots (wallet-store.png), SIGKILLs the pid from the host, relaunches the restore phase, screenshots (wallet-restore.png), compares ownerId/revision/grants/receipts against both the store snapshot and the input, requires clear + empty-after-clear, scans the log for -34018 / missing keychain-access-groups, and writes wallet-summary.txt (wallet_persistence_ok=0|1 plus pids, revisions, force_quit=SIGKILL, match/cleared flags, entitlement error count, log-stream status); every failure mode exits non-zero and never reports ok. (3) simulator-launch-check.sh runs the helper after the plain launch settles (same install, same signature, passes the live pid), fails on helper failure or a missing verdict, and adds wallet_persistence_ok to launch-summary.txt — so the shipping Mac path (`scripts/mac-full-verify.sh` → simulator-launch-check.sh) now carries the store→kill→restore evidence as behaviour. Regression-first: scripts/tests/test_wallet_persistence_check.sh (new, 9 cases with fake PlistBuddy/codesign/xcrun modelling launch pids, a fake Keychain that survives SIGKILL, promise-envelope results, screenshots and the log stream) and two new cases + wallet assertions in scripts/tests/test_simulator_launch_check.sh were committed first (4ea5325f) and fail on BASE_SHA (exit 1 each), then the implementation (9ef411a3) makes them pass.
